name: Saffron-Requiem
description: Saffron-Requiem burns in shades of its name: sulfur-yellow plains, orange lava rivers braiding between three active supervolcanoes, and at the south pole a wound in the world where the crust tore away entirely, leaving the incandescent core exposed to space. Around that second sun stretch glass plains thousands of kilometers wide, fused smooth by whatever cataclysm opened the planet up.

The toxic air glows faintly amber near the vents and eats unprotected metal in hours; sound is a constant low hiss of escaping gas, punctuated by the deep organ-notes of caldera collapse. Ash falls upward here, riding thermal columns into the upper haze, so that it snows in reverse across the whole southern hemisphere.

Microbial mats thrive in the hot acidic springs—organisms that should not exist, their genetics reading as if assembled rather than evolved—and they cluster thickest inside the radiation hotspots, where background counts would kill a human in minutes. Survey probes have mapped geometric regularities beneath the glass: straight lines meeting at nodes, too long and too old to be mining works. The lines all converge on the exposed core.

Uranium lodes around the calderas are the richest ever surveyed, and core-plasma taps could power a battlefleet; three syndicates already auction drilling rights they do not hold. But the last two automated rigs shut themselves down within hours, logs citing containment failures that never occurred, and the microbes keep spreading along the ancient buried lines—outward, toward the equator.
